parsed.why: The national passport and entry rules and government-facility restrictions apply directly. No distinct local hostile layer is documented, but national control makes local protections fragile; the low-risk label is not evidence those exposures are remedied.

Operating public-accommodation protections, gender-identity hate-crime coverage, and enforceable shield laws materially improve the visitor-facing picture. The severe national document and entry regime remains, so this is safer than the national baseline, not low risk.

Public-accommodation and hate-crime protections help, and no adult-facing facility ban is documented. School restrictions and uncertain reversal are a lesser local concern; national document and entry exposures remain decisive.

Birth-sex facility rules cover government buildings and schools, with a reporting and complaint process and a documentation-based defence that may not work for visitors. This universal state-imposed exposure adds materially to the national risks.

The local facility restriction is aimed at students, including in higher education, rather than visitors generally; its prison-treatment rule is resident-facing. These add some local risk, but the national visitor-facing exposures remain the main concern.
